title: intermittent-throughput-firehose-scratch
content:
Notes to self: intermittent throughput regressions under production-ish load (user-sim job). Scratchpad of commands, quick checks, and hypotheses.

TL;DR:
- Regression started showing on 2025-02-08 after config push (autoscale/batcher defaults changed).
- Symptoms: 10–30% lower tokens/sec on p99-latency sensitive routes, occasional batch sizes collapse to 1 even though concurrency high.
- Suspected culprits: continuous-batcher window misconfiguration, stale KV-prefetch disabled on certain model flavors, and an unexpected affinity change on k8s nodes (pack/unpack forcing serialization).

Repro steps (always flaky):
1) Run local load generator: python tools/load_gen.py --model redwood-4x --qps 120 --seq-len 512 --clients 40
   - Observed: throughput 750 tps normally, drops to ~520 tps after ~3m.
2) With same generator but set --batch-window-ms 40 (was 20), throughput stable.
3) Toggle KV prefetch via feature flag: KV_PREFETCH=true/false (env override in container) — when false, immediate throughput drop and many single-token batches seen.

Commands I ran (copy-paste to re-run quickly):
- kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=continuous-batcher -o wide
- kubectl logs -n serving $(kubectl get pod -n serving -l app=continuous-batcher -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -c batcher --since=10m | grep -i "batch size" -A2
- curl -sS 'http://metrics.internal:9090/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(batch_size[5m])' | jq '.'
- promql check (in grafana): rate(requests_total{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[1m]) / avg_over_time(batch_size[1m])
- docker exec -it runtime-container /bin/bash 
  then: ps aux | grep kv_prefetch

Key logs / snippets (sanitized):
- 2025-02-09T03:12:41Z batcher INFO "emitted batch" details={size:1, window_ms:20, wait_ms:21, caller_q:9}
- 2025-02-09T03:12:41Z batcher WARN "window undershoot" target_ms=20 observed=4
- 2025-02-09T03:14:02Z runtime ERROR "kv prefetch failed" model=redwood-4x err="prefetch disabled by policy: flavor=low-latency"
- 2025-02-09T03:14:03Z serving WARN "fallback to small-quant variant" selected=redwood-4x-q8

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Batch window heuristics changed flags in last deploy (config PR 914) — new default reduces max window under high concurrency causing more frequent micro-batches. Evidence: when I increase window_ms manually, throughput recovers.
2) KV prefetch gating logic: a policy gate disables prefetch for certain workload labels. Prefetch off -> more cache misses -> runtime spends cycles reconstructing KV -> batcher stalls -> small batches. Logs show prefetch disabled around regression onset.
3) Autoscaler/affinity churn: pods being moved cause cold caches and sudden serialization on model load. Less likely: no big node drain events in node events.
4) Quantization fallback: selecting q8 variant increases per-token time; combined with micro-batching leads to worse overall throughput.

Quick experiments to run (priority order):
- Experiment A (high confidence): increase batch-window-ms to 40 in staging and reproduce load for 10 min. Collect avg batch size, tps, and p99 latency.
- Experiment B: force KV_PREFETCH=true env and measure throughput under same load.
- Experiment C: pin model to non-quantized flavor (redwood-4x-fp16) to see delta.
- Experiment D: metric correlation script: correlate batch_size, model_variant, node_affinity events over time window.

Prometheus queries I used / want to add:
- avg_over_time(batcher_emitted_batch_size[1m])
- sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_count{route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (instance)
- histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
- increase(node_events_count[30m]) by (reason) -- to check drains

Observations from quick scans:
- avg batch size dips from ~18 to ~3 when regression hits.
- CPU on runtime increases slightly (~10%) but GPU utilization drops ~8% — indicates underutilized GPU due to smaller batches.
- p99 latency spikes correspond to times where batch size collapses.

Config diffs to inspect: (checkpointed locally)
- config/batcher/defaults.yaml @ deploy-2025-02-05 vs deploy-2025-02-08
  - old: max_window_ms: 80, target_window_ms: 25, min_batch_size: 8
  - new: max_window_ms: 50, target_window_ms: 20, min_batch_size: 1  <-- suspicious

Notes on potential quick mitigations (for on-call):
- Emergency revert of batcher default (roll back to previous config) — low-risk, immediate mitigation.
- Hotfix: set min_batch_size to 4 for latency-sensitive routes via route override in routing-config.
- Force enable KV prefetch on affected model flavors through runtime env patch.

Things to watch if we patch:
- Check for increased tail latency from larger windows under bursty traffic (could increase latency for single-user interactive cases).
- Monitor GPU queueing and memory pressure when batch windows grow.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Who approved PR 914? (check PR history + reviewer list) -> flagged to Samira for context.
- Why was min_batch_size set to 1? Was there a reason for edge-cases? (search GH comments)
- Are there telemetry gaps for the batcher decision path? I want a sampling trace for decisions when window undershoot occurs.

Useful Slack threads / links: (copy-paste later)
- #serving-runtime: message ts 1707512345 (contains initial alert)
- PR discussion: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/914 (config change)
- Ticket: JIRA-RDW-4873 (incident page)

Quick checklist for next 24h: 
- [ ] Run Experiment A in staging and collect traces (owner: Priya).
- [ ] If success, prepare rollback patch and run canary (owner: Samira).
- [ ] Add metric for batcher_decision_reason to runtime logs (owner: Ethan).
- [ ] Draft postmortem stub and timeline in JIRA (owner: Priya).

Random notes / scribbles:
- Could also be related to client-side concurrency drop: client may backpressure incorrectly -> server sees weird arrival patterns -> batcher reacts. Need to look at ingress TPS histograms.
- Check connection keepalive settings on envoy -> if connections reset, batcher gets short-lived streams -> smaller batches.

End of scratch — will update after running the three experiments.
